Versus
Mrs. Lutfunnahar Begum and others ------ Opposite parties
full_judgment:
Mr. Sheikh Abdul Awal, J:- This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-3 to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 5.01.2006 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 7th Court, Dhaka in Civil Revision No.531 of 2004 arising out of Artha Rin Adalat Case No.388 of 2003 should not be set-aside. 

2. The relevant facts in short are that the-petitioner-Bank as plaintiff instituted a suit being Artha Rin Suit No.388 of 2003 against the defendant-opposite party No.1, Mrs. Lutfunnahar and another for realisation of its outstanding dues with 'interest amounting to Tk. 25,87,984/- as stood on 31.3.2003 on the averments that the loan amounting to Tk.2,00,000/- was disbursed as per terms and conditions of loan sanction letter but the defendant-opposite parties inspite of repeated letters to re-pay the loan issued by the plaintiff-bank did not turn to repay the loan. Hence, the suit. 

3. After exhausting all the formalities available under the law the suit was decreed ex-parte vide ex-parte order and decree dated 4.10.2003 (decree singed on 13.10.2003) and subsequently, the final decree was drawn up on 01.01.2004. Ultimately, the decree-holder-Bank in order to realise its outstanding dues by selling the mortgaged property put the decree into execution by filing Artha Jari Case No.61 of 2004 before the Artha Rin Adalat, 1st Court, Dhaka. 

4. During the pendency of the said Artha Jail Case No.61 of 2004 before the Artha Rin Adalat, 1st  Court, Dhaka the judgment-debtors filed an application under section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 for dismissing the Artha Jari Case. 

5. The Artha Rin Adalat upon hearing the parties rejected the application by its Order No. 16 dated 17.10.2004 holding that the provision of section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003 is not applicable in the case inasmuch as in this case the suit was decreed ex-parte vide ex-parte order and decree dated 4.10.2003 (decree singed on 13.10.2003) and the final decree was drawn up on 01.01.2004, that is, long before the provision of section 47(3) came into force. 

6. Against the said order No. 16 dated 17.10.2004 the defendant-opposite parties filed Civil Revision No.531 of 2004 in the Court of District Judge, Dhaka. Ultimately, the said revision was transmitted to the Court of Additional District Judge, 7th Court, Dhaka for disposal. 

7. The learned Additional District Judge upon hearing the revisional application by his judgment and order dated 5.01.2006 allowed the revision and set-aside the ex-parte order and decree dated 04.102003 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat in Artha Rin Suit No.388 of 2003. 

8. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order dated 5.01.2006 the decree-holder bank moved this Court and obtained the present Rule.  

9. Mr. Kazi Behan Nabi, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the learned Additional District Judge under misconception of law and facts most illegally without adverting the material finding of the Artha Rin Adalat, that is, the provision of section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is not applicable in the case most illegally passed the impugned judgment and order dated 5.01.2006 setting aside the ex-party order and decree dated 4.10.2003. He next submits that the learned Additional District Judge ought to have been arrived at a finding that the revisional application was misconceived, ill-advised and not maintainable inasmuch as the judgment debtors preferred the same against the ex-parte judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat without depositing 10% of the decreetal amount as per express provision of sub-section 3 to section 19 of the Ain, 2003. 
10. Referring to the provisions of section 47(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003 Mr. Rehan Nabi, submits that the learned Additional District Judge failed to appreciate the simple question of law as the provisions of section 47 of the Ain, 2003 is not applicable in the present case inasmuch as the Artha Rin Suit No.388 of 2003 was decreed on 4.10.2003 ( decree singed on 13.10.2003) and the final decree was drawn up on 01.01.2004 that is long before the provision of section 47 of the Ain, 2003 came into force on 5th May, 2004. Mr. Rehan, finally submits that in the facts and circumstances of the case the impugned judgment and order is not only illegal also perverse being contrary to law as well as without jurisdiction and as such the same is liable to be set-aside.  

11. On the other hand, Mr. Mohammad Abdullah, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties supports the impugned judgment and order passed by the Additional District Judge, 7th  Court, Dhaka which was, according to him just, correct and proper. He submits that the suit was decreed ex-parte against the judgment-debtor-opposite parties for an amount of Tk.25,00,000/- but there is nothing on record to show that the claim of the plaintiff-Bank is based on any documentary evidence whatsoever. He further submits that as per provision of section 60(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 all suit pending under the old Artha Rin AM namely Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 stood transferred before the Artha Rin Adalat established under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and in such legal position the Bank cannot claim more than 200% of the principal amount as per provision of section 47 of the Ain, 2003 and thus, the learned Additional District Judge committed no illegality in setting aside the ex-party judgment and decree dated 4.10.2003 (decree singed on 13.10.2003).

12. We have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides and perused the Revisional application, supplementary affidavit dated 17.8.2010 along with other connected papers including the impugned judgment and order as filed therewith. To appreciate the submissions of the learned Advocates of both the sides from a correct angle, we want to decide first as to the question of maintainability of the instant revisional application. 

13. In deciding this point, we feel it necessary to quote hereunder the provisions of section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. 

Section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003 reads as follows:  ১৯। একতরফা ডিক্রী সম্পর্কিত বিধান ৷-
১ ৷ মামলার শুনানীর জন্য ধার্য কোন তারিখে বিবাদী আদালতে অনুপস্থিত থাকিলে, কিৎবা মামলা শুনানীর জন্য গৃহীত হইবার পর ডাকিয়া বিবাদীকে উপস্থিত পাওয়া না গেলে, আদালত মামলা একতরফা সূত্রে নিস্পত্তি করিবে। 

২ ৷ কোন মামলা একতরফা সূত্রে ডিক্রী হইলে, বিবাদী উক্ত একতরফা ডিক্রীর তারিখের অথবা উক্ত একতরফা ডিক্রী সম্পর্কে অবগত হইবার ৩০ (ত্রিশ) দিবসের মধ্যে, উপ-ধারা (৩) এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে, উক্ত একতরফা ডিক্রী রদের জন্য দরখাস্ত করিতে পারিবেন ৷

৩ ৷ উপ-ধারা (২) এর বিধান অনুযায়ী দরখাস্ত দাখিলের ক্ষেত্রে বিবাদীকে উক্ত দরখাস্ত দাখিলের তারিখের পরবর্তী ১৫ (পনের) দিবসের মধ্যে ডিক্রীকৃত অর্থের ১ ০% এর সমপরিমান টাকা বাদীর সেই পরিমাণের জন্য স্বীকৃতিস্বরূপ নগদ সংশ্লিষ্ট আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানে, অথবা জামানত স্বরূপ ব্যাৎক ড্রাফট, পে-অর্ডার বা অন্য কোন প্রকার নগদায়নযোপ্য বিনিমেয় দলিল (Negotiable Instrument) আকারে জামানত হিসাবে আদালতে জমাদান করিতে হইবে।

8।উপ-ধারা(৩)এর বিধানমতে ডিক্রীকৃত অর্থের ১০% এর সমপরিমান টাকা জমাদানের সংগে সংগে দরখাস্তটি মঞ্জুর হইবে, একতরফা ডিক্রী রদ হইবে এবং মূল মামলা উহার পূর্বের নম্বর ও নথিতে পুনরুজ্জীবিত হইবে এবং আদালত ঐ মর্মে একটি আদেশ লিপিবদ্ধ করিবে, এবং অতঃপর মামলাটি যে পর্যায়ে এক তরফা নিষ্পত্তি হইয়াছিল, ঐ পর্যায়ের অব্যবহিত পূর্ববর্তী পর্যায় হইতে পরিচালিত হইবে৷ 

From a reading of the above quoted provisions of section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003, it transpires that Artha Rin Adalat AM imposes two preconditions on filing an application against the ex-parte decree of the Artha Rin Adalat. One of such preconditions is that 10% of the decreetal amount as security must be deposited and then the application must be filed within 30 days from the date of knowledge of the ex-parte decree. It is found in this case the present opposite parties preferred the t revisional application against the ex-parte judgment and decree before the learned District Judge, Dhaka without depositing any amount in compliance with the provision of section 19 of the Ain, 2003. Since the defendant judgment debtors had not deposited 10% of the decreetal amount for preferring the application or revision against the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat, in the eye of law the application/ revision was incompetent and not maintainable. 

14. Now, let us see how far the Artha Rin Adalat was justified in rejecting the application under section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003. The Artha Rin Adalat rejected the application under section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 by its Order No.16 dated 17.10.2004 stating as follows: 

“অর্থঋণ আদালত আইন ২০০৩ এর ৪৭(৩)ধারায় বলা হইয়াছে এই ধারার বিধানটি এই আইন বলবৎ হইবার ১(এক) বৎসর পর কার্যকর হইবে৷ আলোচ্য ক্ষেত্রে দেখা যায় অর্থঋণ আদালত আইন ২০০৩ এর ১লা যে, ২০০৩ হইতে কার্যকর হইয়াছে এবং 8৭ ধারাটি ১লা মে, ২০০8 হইতে কার্যকর হইয়াছে৷ ফলে দেখা যায় বর্নিত 8৭ ধারার কার্যকরী হওয়ার বহুপূর্বে অর্থ্যাৎ ৪/১০/২০০৩ ইং তারিখে অত্র মোকদ্দমা একতরফা ডিক্রীর আদেশ হওয়ায় বিবাদীর ৪৭ ধারার দরখাস্তটি বিধি সম্মত নহে৷ এমতাবস্হায় বিবাদীপক্ষের বিগত ১৫/৯/২০০8 ইং তারিখের দরখাস্তটি সরাসরি নাকোচ করা হইল৷” 

15. On a perusal of the said order together with the provisions of section 47 of the AM, 2003, it appears that sub-sections (1) and (2) of section 47 of the AM, 2003 has put an embargo on a filing suit claiming interest more than 200% of the loan granted and sub-section (3) of section 47 of the Ain, 2003 has made this embargo affective from one year after coming of this Ain, 2003 into force, that is, from 1st May, 2004. Our, view is therefore, that the Artha Rin Adalat rightly on assigning sound reason rejected the application under section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 by its order No.16 dated 17.10.2004. 

16. On an analysis of the impugned judgment and order dated 5.01.2006, we are surprise to see that the learned Additional District Judge without adverting the 'sole finding of the Artha Rin Adalat that the provision of section 47(3) of the Ain, 2003 is not applicable in this case abruptly set-aside the ex-party order and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat. We do not think that the learned Additional District Judge sitting under revisional jurisdiction made a correct approach to the simple problem. 

17. Furthermore, there is another aspect of the case to which we think the attention of 
the learned Additional District Judge ought to have been drawn that is the proposition of law is by now well settled in so many cases including in the case of Sultana Jute Mills Ltd. and others Vs. Agrani Bank and others repotted in 46 DLR(AD)174, in the case of Hosne Ara Begum & another Vs. Islami Bank Bangladesh and others reported in 5 MLR(AD) 290, in the case of Md. Harun-Or-Rashid Vs. Pubali Bank Ltd. and others reported in 27 BLD(AD) 326 that no revision lies against the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat. Therefore, we find there is a good deal of substance in the contentions raised by Mr. Rehan Nabi, that the learned Additional District Judge under misconception of law and facts most illegally set-aside the ex-parte judgment and decree and the same is liable to be set-aside.
18. On query from the Court Mr. Abdullah, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties could not refer to any principle which has been allegedly violated by the Artha Rin Adalat or to any fact which has either been ignored or wrongly relied upon. Mr. Abdullah, however, repeatedly submitted that the Artha Rin Adalat mechanically decreed the suit ex-parte without considering the aspect that the present opposite parties paid Tk. 1,72,000/- out of total Tk. 2,00,000/- principal amount. 

19. This argument in defending the impugned judgment and order dated 5.01.2006 is fallacious as well as misconceived. 

20. In any view of the matter, having regard to the fact as aforesaid, we are inclined to hold that the learned Additional District Judge seriously erred in law in passing the impugned order without properly applying his judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case and law bearing on the subject and the same has resulted in an error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. 

21. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned judgment and order dated 5.01.2006 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 7th Court, Dhaka in Civil Revision No.531 of 2004 arising out of Artha Rin Adalat Case No.388 of 2003 is set-aside. 

22. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court stands vacated. 

23. Since the matter has been dragging over of period of 7 years the Artha Rin Adalat concerned is directed to proceed with the execution case expeditiously. 

24. Communicate the order at once. 

End.
